audit_summary: All 11 facts are directly supported by the cited repository files.

facts.statement: The command-line option `--setup-show` enables displaying fixture setup while tests execute.
During fixture setup, setup-show stores the raw `request.param` as `fixturedef.cached_param` when the fixture has no custom IDs.
When custom fixture IDs exist, setup-show stores either the callable ID result or the indexed explicit ID instead of the raw parameter.
The setup-show output path interpolates `fixturedef.cached_param` with `"[{}]".format(...)`, which invokes ordinary string formatting on the parameter.
The cached parameter is rendered for both setup and teardown because teardown calls the same `_show_fixture_action` function before deleting `cached_param`.
Existing setup-show parameter coverage uses string values `foo` and `bar` and expects those values in setup and teardown output.
Existing setup-show coverage separately verifies explicit string IDs `spam` and `ham`.
Existing setup-show coverage also verifies callable IDs that transform string parameters to `FOO` and `BAR`.
The repository already provides `saferepr`, documented as returning a size-limited representation that handles failures in user `repr` implementations and generally avoids raising exceptions.
`saferepr` is already used in parameter-related validation to display an invalid ID value safely.
The parameter-ID generation code explicitly accepts bytes and contains a TODO noting that returning bytes can leave code paths that probably do not handle them.
